issues.title: Nested test delegate missing final modifier
issues.description: The rule requires that classes not designed for subclassing must be marked with the 'final' keyword to prevent unintended inheritance and enable compiler optimizations. The FakeWKNavigationDelegate class is a test utility not intended for inheritance but lacks the 'final' modifier.
issues.rule_name: Classes That Should Not Be Subclassed Must Be Marked Final

issues.title: Wrong frame captured in navigation delegate
issues.description: The delegate captures navigationAction.targetFrame instead of navigationAction.sourceFrame. The targetFrame represents the frame that will be navigated (which may be nil for new windows), while sourceFrame represents the frame that initiated the navigation. This causes the helper to capture nil or incorrect frame information, breaking all tests that depend on valid WKFrameInfo objects. The original intent was to capture the frame initiating the navigation request.

issues.title: Ignoring XCTWaiter result allows returning stale data on timeout
issues.description: The captureFrameAndOrigin method no longer checks if waiter == .completed before returning captured values. This means the function will return potentially nil or incomplete frame and origin data even when the expectation times out or is interrupted. The function may return cached/partial data from a failed navigation attempt, causing tests to use invalid WebKit objects and producing false test results.

issues.title: Test expectation fulfilled after wait causes timeout
issues.description: The expectation.fulfill() call was moved outside the decisionHandler closure and placed after the wait() call. This creates a logic error where the test waits for an expectation that will never be fulfilled by the decision handler. The expectation is only fulfilled after the wait times out, causing the test to always fail with a timeout error rather than validating the actual permission decision behavior.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #31309 - Bugfix FXIOS-14456 #31308 ⁃ Fix test failing on XCode 26.2 to enable using this version on Bitrise

structured_output.summary:
The PR deletes the `MockWKFrameInfo` and `MockWKSecurityOrigin` subclasses, which crash under the Xcode 26.2 WebKit SDK. In their place it adds `WebKitTestHelpers.captureFrameAndOrigin(for:)`. That helper loads a URL in a real `WKWebView` and grabs the `WKFrameInfo` and `WKSecurityOrigin` that WebKit passes to `decidePolicyFor navigationAction`. The three media-capture tests in `WKUIHandlerTests` now use those real objects. Moving off the alloc-hack mocks is the right call.

`testRequestMediaCaptureSuccess` is broken, though. Its `decisionHandler` no longer calls `expectation.fulfill()`. The `fulfill()` call was moved to the line after `wait(for:)`, so it can only run after the wait has already returned. `wait(for:)` with no timeout defaults to `.infinity`, so this test hangs or stalls CI instead of passing. There are also some smaller issues in the helper: an unused `waiter` binding, a timeout result that gets thrown away, `.allow` letting a real request go out to example.com, and a short 3s timeout for a cold WebKit process on CI.
structured_output.verdictRationale: `testRequestMediaCaptureSuccess` never fulfills its expectation before waiting on it, so with the default `.infinity` timeout it hangs instead of passing. The PR's goal is to get the test suite passing on Xcode 26.2, so this has to be fixed before merge.

architecture.overview:
`DefaultUIHandler` (WKUIHandler.swift) implements `WKUIDelegate.webView(_:requestMediaCapturePermissionFor:initiatedByFrame:type:decisionHandler:)`. It calls `decisionHandler(.prompt)` when the handler is active and the session delegate grants permission, and `.deny` otherwise. It never reads the origin or frame. The tests used to pass hand-made `WKSecurityOrigin`/`WKFrameInfo` subclasses. Those crash under the new SDK because WebKit now expects fully initialized internal state.

The PR adds a test utility, `WebKitTestHelpers`, which creates a real `WKWebView`, attaches a `FakeWKNavigationDelegate`, starts a load, and blocks with `XCTWaiter` until `decidePolicyFor navigationAction` fires. It then returns `navigationAction.targetFrame` and its `securityOrigin`. Those real objects are passed straight into the handler under test.
steps: Start at `DefaultUIHandler.webView(_:requestMediaCapturePermissionFor:...)` in WKUIHandler.swift (lines 167-177). This is the code under test. It calls `decisionHandler` synchronously.
Read `WebKitTestHelpers.captureFrameAndOrigin(for:timeout:)`. It creates a `WKWebView`, sets `FakeWKNavigationDelegate`, calls `load`, and waits on an `XCTestExpectation` through `XCTWaiter`.
`FakeWKNavigationDelegate.webView(_:decidePolicyFor:decisionHandler:)` captures `targetFrame` and `securityOrigin`, allows the navigation, and fulfills the expectation.
In `WKUIHandlerTests`, each media-capture test calls the helper first, then passes the captured `(frame, origin)` to the subject and waits for its decision handler expectation.
The old `MockWKFrameInfo` and `MockWKSecurityOrigin` files are deleted. Nothing else in the repo references them.

findings.title: testRequestMediaCaptureSuccess waits on an expectation nothing fulfills, so it hangs
findings.body:
The PR changes how this test fulfills its expectation, and the new version can't pass:

::diff{file="BrowserKit/Tests/WebEngineTests/WKUIHandlerTests.swift" lines="43-54"}

- The `decisionHandler` closure no longer calls `expectation.fulfill()`. It couldn't anyway, because `expectation` is now declared after the closure.
- `expectation.fulfill()` was moved below `wait(for: [expectation])`, so it runs only after the wait has returned.
- `XCTestCase.wait(for:)` with no explicit timeout defaults to `.infinity`. `DefaultUIHandler` calls `decisionHandler(.prompt)` synchronously, but nothing ever fulfills the expectation.

::callout{type="warning"}
This test hangs until CI kills it, or until the test-plan execution time allowance fires. That defeats the PR's goal of getting the suite green on Xcode 26.2. The `XCTAssertEqual(decision, .prompt)` check still runs, but its outcome never reaches a passing test.

Use the same pattern as the other two tests:

::suggestion{file="BrowserKit/Tests/WebEngineTests/WKUIHandlerTests.swift" lines="43-54"}
        let expectation = expectation(description: "Wait for the decision handler to be called")
        let decisionHandler = { (decision: WKPermissionDecision) in
            XCTAssertEqual(decision, .prompt)
            expectation.fulfill()
        }

        subject.webView(MockWKWebView(),
                        requestMediaCapturePermissionFor: origin,
                        initiatedByFrame: frame,
                        type: .cameraAndMicrophone,
                        decisionHandler: decisionHandler)
        wait(for: [expectation])
findings.fixPrompt: In `BrowserKit/Tests/WebEngineTests/WKUIHandlerTests.swift`, `testRequestMediaCaptureSuccess` (lines 43-54) never fulfills its expectation before `wait(for:)`. The `fulfill()` call is placed after the wait, and the decisionHandler closure doesn't call it, so the test hangs with the default infinite timeout. Declare `let expectation = expectation(...)` before the `decisionHandler` closure, call `expectation.fulfill()` inside the closure after `XCTAssertEqual(decision, .prompt)`, and delete the `expectation.fulfill()` line after `wait(for: [expectation])`. Match the structure of `testRequestMediaCaptureIsActiveFalse` in the same file.

findings.title: Helper ignores the XCTWaiter result and allows a real network load, which invites flaky failures
findings.fixPrompt: In `BrowserKit/Tests/WebEngineTests/Utilities/WebKitTestHelpers.swift`: (1) in `FakeWKNavigationDelegate.webView(_:decidePolicyFor:decisionHandler:)` (line 26), call `decisionHandler(.cancel)` instead of `.allow`. The frame and origin are already captured, so no real network load to example.com is needed. (2) At line 45, replace the unused `let waiter =` binding with a check of the `XCTWaiter.Result`, and return nil (or note the timeout) when it isn't `.completed`. (3) Raise the default timeout from 3.0 to something more CI-tolerant, such as 10 seconds. Optionally set `expect.assertForOverFulfill = false`, or guard against fulfilling more than once.

findings.title: WebKitTestHelpers creates a WKWebView from a nonisolated context
findings.fixPrompt: In `BrowserKit/Tests/WebEngineTests/Utilities/WebKitTestHelpers.swift`, annotate `WebKitTestHelpers` and its nested `FakeWKNavigationDelegate` with `@MainActor`, since they create and delegate for a `WKWebView`, which is main-actor isolated. This matches `DefaultTestDependencies.swift` in the same folder. Check that `WKUIHandlerTests` (already `@MainActor`) still compiles.

findings.title: Replacing the alloc-hack mocks with real WebKit objects is the right direction
findings.body: The old `MockWKSecurityOrigin` used `perform(NSSelectorFromString("alloc"))` to get around an unavailable initializer. It depended on WebKit internals and was bound to break, and it did on the Xcode 26.2 SDK. Capturing real `WKFrameInfo` and `WKSecurityOrigin` from a navigation is the right way to make these tests hold up against future SDK changes. The deleted mocks had no other users in the repo, so removing them is safe. The doc comment on `WebKitTestHelpers` also explains clearly why the helper exists.
